def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Finds the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using a modified 
    heap approach to maintain a min-heap of the k largest elements. 
    Time complexity: O(n log k).
    """

    import heapq

    # Create a min-heap with the first k elements
    min_heap = nums[:k]
    heapq.heapify(min_heap)

    # Process the remaining elements
    for num in nums[k:]:
        if num > min_heap[0]:
            heapq.heappop(min_heap)
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, num)

    # The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element
    return min_heap[0]

def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Finds the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using the Quickselect 
    algorithm, which is a selection algorithm to find the k-th smallest element. 
    Time complexity: O(n) on average, O(n^2) in the worst case.
    """
    
    import random

    def partition(left: int, right: int, pivot_index: int) -> int:
        pivot_value = nums[pivot_index]
        # Move pivot to the end
        nums[pivot_index], nums[right] = nums[right], nums[pivot_index]
        store_index = left
        for i in range(left, right):
            if nums[i] > pivot_value:  # Note: for k-th largest, we use >
                nums[store_index], nums[i] = nums[i], nums[store_index]
                store_index += 1
        # Move pivot to its final place
        nums[right], nums[store_index] = nums[store_index], nums[right]
        return store_index

    def quickselect(left: int, right: int, k: int) -> int:
        if left == right:  # If the list contains only one element
            return nums[left]
        
        pivot_index = random.randint(left, right)
        pivot_index = partition(left, right, pivot_index)

        if k == pivot_index:
            return nums[k]
        elif k < pivot_index:
            return quickselect(left, pivot_index - 1, k)
        else:
            return quickselect(pivot_index + 1, right, k)

    return quickselect(0, len(nums) - 1, k - 1)  # k-1 for zero-based index

def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Finds the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using a Min-Heap approach. 
    It maintains a heap of size k to efficiently track the k largest elements. 
    Time complexity: O(n log k).
    """
    
    import heapq
    
    if k <= 0 or k > len(nums):
        raise ValueError("k should be between 1 and the length of the list.")
    
    # Create a min-heap of the first k elements
    min_heap = nums[:k]
    heapq.heapify(min_heap)
    
    # Process the rest of the elements in the list
    for num in nums[k:]:
        # Only add to the heap if the new number is larger than the smallest in heap
        if num > min_heap[0]:
            heapq.heappop(min_heap)  # Remove the smallest element
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, num)  # Push the new number into the heap

    return min_heap[0]  # The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element
